findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_integration.py:843-844 passes lease descriptors only to the configured command. A Python command that subsequently uses ordinary subprocess.run closes those descriptors while retaining DEV_PLATFORM_MACHINE_POOL_LEASE. Existing wrappers such as template/scripts/openspec_lifecycle.py:524 do exactly this. A nested pooled runner then fails at machine_pool.py:623-624; a child that does not inspect the lease can continue without holding tokens after its ancestors die. The orphan regression test covers only a child explicitly launched with pass_fds (tests/test_machine_pool.py:55).
findings.summary: Descriptor inheritance requires cooperation from every subprocess wrapper, so the documented protection does not cover arbitrary validation descendants.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/machine_pool.py:606-610 checks that fds is a list of nonnegative integers but does not require its length to match weight or require distinct descriptors. Lines 614-625 check only os.fstat, and lines 640-645 then bypass acquisition. Consequently, a lease payload with pooled=true, weight=4 and fds=[] runs without holding any tokens even when a pool is configured.
findings.summary: Nested lease validation accepts an empty descriptor list or unrelated open descriptors as proof of a pooled lease.
